subject: Packaging decision: modular safety-net vs reserved throughput — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Anya Reddy <anya@clearpath.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, May 5, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Packaging questions — seats vs throughput and credit ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from my side as we prepare internal sponsor materials:

1) We need a clear comparison between a) buying reserved throughput (dedicated capacity) versus b) remaining on hosted with modular feature bundles and one-time surge credits. Our key constraints are predictable monthly cost and keeping latency SLAs for customers on our edge tier.

2) If we move forward with option (b), procurement will ask for an explicit credit/concession for our first renewal as a guardrail — can you tell me what flexibility you have there?

Attached is a small usage forecast for May–Jul (anonymized). Happy to jump on a quick call — is Thursday afternoon your availability?

Thanks,
Anya
Head of Platform
ClearPath AI

Attachment: ClearPath_usage_forecast_May2026.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Reddy <anya@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, May 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM -07:00
Subject: RE: Packaging questions — seats vs throughput and credit ask

Hi Anya —

Thanks for the forecast and the clear ask. High level: we can support both approaches; tradeoffs below. I attached a single-page proposal to make it concrete.

Option A — Reserved throughput (Dedicated):
- Pros: Predictable monthly bill, guaranteed throughput, easier to diagnose latency incidents since capacity is isolated.
- Cons: Higher baseline commitment; longer lead time for extra capacity.

Option B — Hosted + Modular bundles + Surge credits:
- Pros: Lower baseline commitment, simpler account setup, flexibility to toggle feature bundles to control token cost.
- Cons: Less deterministic throughput at peak unless you accept surge-credit limits; marginally higher per-token cost at scale.

Suggestion: For your May–Jul forecast, a hybrid plan often works: reserve a baseline throughput that covers 70–80% of normal traffic, keep a modular hosting route for experimental endpoints, and provide a one-time surge credit pool to cover exceptional spikes.

I've attached RWI_ModularSafetyNet_Proposal_v1.pdf and a pricing_model_spreadsheet.xlsx that maps forecast rows to estimated monthly cost under each approach.

If that aligns, I can propose a concession matrix (one-time credits tied to renewal and usage tiers) and loop in Neha from commercial to confirm approval levels.

I have a slot Thursday 2:00–2:30pm PT — does that work?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RWI_ModularSafetyNet_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, 120KB); pricing_model_spreadsheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, May 6, 2026 at 8:15 AM -07:00
Subject: RE: Packaging questions — seats vs throughput and credit ask

Anya / Marissa —

Quick operational notes from infra side:
- If you choose Reserved (Option A), we recommend sizing around p95 token throughput per minute rather than average to avoid cold-start degradation. That maps to roughly 1.8x your reported peak in the sheet.
- If you go Hosted modular (Option B) + surge credits, we should define an automatic fallback policy: when hosted latency breaches 500ms for more than 3 consecutive minutes, route non-critical traffic to the lower-cost variant or throttle non-essential endpoints. We can include that as a policy in the SLA addendum.

Questions for sizing: can you provide the split of requests by endpoint (inference-heavy vs metadata-only) and % of synchronous API calls vs async batch? That will materially change which option is cheaper.

Sharing HubSpot deal so we can keep notes: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/CP-2026-0047

—Ben

Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, May 6, 2026 at 1:40 PM -07:00
Subject: RE: Packaging questions — seats vs throughput and credit ask

Thanks Ben — helpful.

Answers to your sizing Qs:
- Endpoint split: 60% inference-heavy (customer-facing), 40% metadata & batch (background).
- Sync vs async: ~85% synchronous.

Procurement flagged that for any hybrid approach they'll expect a 10–15% credit applied to the first renewal if we commit to multi-quarter purchase in year one. Can Redwood accommodate a 10% first-renewal credit if we sign a 12-month term now?

We'd like to lock the Thursday 2:00pm PT slot if that's still open — agenda: walk through the proposal, finalize the concession, and confirm DocuSign flow.

Best,
Anya

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, May 7, 2026 at 9:00 AM -07:00
Subject: Internal: concession matrix suggestion for ClearPath

Marissa / Ben —

Internal note before our call with ClearPath: procurement's 10–15% ask is reasonable if we calibrate with usage tiers and guardrails. Proposed matrix:

- 12-month committed term -> 10% one-time credit applied at renewal if usage meets >= 75% of committed throughput over the first 10 months.
- 24-month committed term -> 12% one-time credit applied at renewal with 70% usage threshold and a customer success-run enablement plan.
- Short-term pilots (<=3 months) -> no renewal credit; offer one-time surge credit up to $15k on sign.

Constraints: credits cannot be applied to third-party pass-through fees or marketplace fees; credits are non-transferable. We should also avoid changing SLA permanence — credits are financial concessions only.

Suggested DocuSign clause (for commercial redline):
"""
One-time Renewal Credit: Customer will receive a one-time credit equal to X% of the then-current contract value applied against an invoice issued at the time of Renewal, subject to the usage thresholds defined in Schedule A. Credits are non-refundable and do not alter Redwood's standard SLA provisions.
"""

If you want legal to pre-clear, I can route a short memo to Legal with the matrix and clause. Otherwise I'm happy to present this on the call.

—Neha
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Reddy <anya@clearpath.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, May 7, 2026 at 4:20 PM -07:00
Subject: Final: hybrid packaging recommendation + next steps (DocuSign + onboarding)

Anya / Team —

Thanks for the constructive discussion. Per the call, here's the agreed recommendation and next steps:

Summary recommendation (hybrid):
- Baseline: Reserved throughput sized at ~80% of projected p95 traffic (reduces peak degradation risk).
- Hosted modular tier: Keep experimental endpoints on hosted with feature-bundled controls to limit token spend.
- One-time surge credit pool: $25,000 applied as a credit to first renewal invoice, contingent on signing a 12-month term today. (This maps to the 10% concession band for the expected contract size in the proposal.)

Attachments included: updated proposal PDF and a pricing model that shows month-by-month expected charges under the hybrid configuration.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to send updated DocuSign with the one-time credit clause and the usage threshold (we'll use the language Neha proposed). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/link/Sign?token=XYZ-CP-47
2) ClearPath procurement to sign — target by 05/14/2026 to hit May billing cycle.
3) Post-sign: schedule a technical onboarding call (Ben to lead) in the first week after signing.

If procurement needs a slightly higher credit we can escalate to revenue ops, but this is our baseline approved concession for a 12-month commitment.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
